faqs.question: Where should a company start if it has no defined AI project?
faqs.shortAnswer: Start from a process, not from a tool.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The first task is choosing a recurring decision, visible cost or risk worth reducing. The first conversation clarifies whether the right step is consulting, a course, data analysis or a controlled prototype.

faqs.question: How should the first process to improve with AI be chosen?
faqs.shortAnswer: Choose a frequent, observable process linked to a cost or delay.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Good candidates include repeated emails, documents to read, priorities to assign or decisions arriving late. If the process is not observable, it should first be made clearer.

faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, if it starts from decisions, processes and skills before technology.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Many initial activities do not require software development: process mapping, risk criteria, focused training and first-case selection matter first. Technical work arrives only when the scope is clear.

faqs.detailedAnswer: A tool can help, but it does not decide goal, data, responsibility and success criteria. Artik Lab uses the first diagnosis to avoid isolated trials and connect AI to an operating result.

faqs.question: How can a company know whether it is ready to use AI?
faqs.shortAnswer: Readiness depends on process, sponsor, minimum data and clear responsibility.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The company does not need to be mature everywhere. It does need one concrete problem, people able to validate the result and a decision to improve. Otherwise training or mapping should come first.

faqs.question: How should ROI be evaluated for an AI project?
faqs.shortAnswer: Compare current cost, possible improvement and actions that can truly be taken.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Before the model, baseline, KPIs and responsibility are needed. If AI produces a signal but nobody can act, value stays theoretical; if it changes a frequent decision, return can be estimated.

faqs.shortAnswer: Define a stop criterion before the full investment.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Each case should have hypotheses, KPIs, minimum data, responsibility and stop conditions. A negative verdict on data or process can be a good result when it avoids larger costs.

faqs.shortAnswer: No, but the company must know which data exists, who understands it and its limits.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Perfectly clean data rarely exists at the start. The first task can be assessing quality, coverage, errors and usefulness against the decision to improve.
